source_en: A scrap of paper carefully torn from a notebook. It bears the Spacetrek Collective's emblem. A short message is written on the back. I was very curious as to the kind of fortune that healed you, until I found that particular Roya man and asked him a few simple questions. If your old illness ever returns, his seemingly nonsensical remarks might help to stir your memory. I exhausted nearly every means of transport available to reach this remote Royan observation station mentioned in the report. I also confirmed once again that the one who saved her was nothing more than a shabby old man in his twilight years. No conspiracy. No hidden design. Her survival was purely by chance. This Roya also showed me the objects Lucilla had used her ability to read—random trinkets, nothing more. I cannot fathom what magic these objects possessed that allowed Lucilla to escape the hysteria brought on by her ability. Naturally, I would not believe this old man understood memory-type Resonators better than the New Federation's finest doctors. Truly a pointless journey. My interest in this place was spent almost immediately. "Madam, a simple truth, it is. If you only see through a camera lens, only observe through photographs, you will never grasp the cold of the frostlands, nor their vastness." "Don't play coy with me." "I am not. It was President Lucilla who told me this. After she laid her hands on these trivial little objects, she finally understood." "Understood what?" "That life is not a photograph. Life is flesh. Life is blood. Life must not be survived, but lived." "...Lucilla has always chosen her own way of living." "I have a child too. That is why I understand why you fail to see it. Just as I observe the frostlands, President Lucilla observes others. Tell me, have you always watched her the same way you do now?" the Roya asked me. An arrogant question. One that presumed to understand me. I did not answer him.

source_en:
Unlike her brother, Rebecca never planned on becoming an edgerunner. They were both raised by the notorious merc known as Papa Sunrise—their only parent. But while he spent years hammering his legacy into both of them, Rebecca never shared Pilar's stubborn hunger to inherit their father's dream.

She wanted freedom. She wanted cute things. She wanted to find her own dream in Night City... which meant she spent a lot of time butting heads with her old man.

Life doesn't wait for anyone to make up their mind. When Papa Sunrise vanished without a trace, Rebecca and Pilar's lives took a sharp turn for the worse. They found themselves sleeping in the back of a busted-up car—once their father's loyal ride on every gig, now the only inheritance they had left.

It was Wakako, the legendary fixer and long-time associate of their father, who threw them a line—or rather, a gig. She gave them a chance to prove they were worthy of Papa's legacy. But there was still a ways to go before the siblings could truly fit edgerunner-sized shoes.

Just as Papa Sunrise had always warned, Rebecca was too emotional, too unpredictable, and far too hotheaded for Night City. She nearly tanked mission after mission; instead of following simple instructions from her fixer, she always chose to follow her gut. Pilar couldn't stand it, and the two of them would tear into each other after every job. But in the end, despite all the quarreling, she still wanted to help him achieve his dream. 

It wasn't until they fell in with Maine's crew that things finally started to turn around. Rebecca and Pilar's habit of jumping down each other's throats became the crew's daily bread—often a loud, profanity-laced background track to their lives. Others would wonder why they kept hanging out if they hated each other so much.

But deep down, they really cared about each other.
new_translation_vi: Không giống như anh trai mình, Rebecca chưa bao giờ có ý định trở thành một edgerunner. Cả hai đều được nuôi dưỡng bởi tay lính đánh thuê khét tiếng được biết đến với cái tên Papa Sunrise—người cha duy nhất của họ. Nhưng trong khi ông dành nhiều năm để khắc sâu di sản của mình vào cả hai, Rebecca chưa bao giờ chia sẻ sự khao khát bướng bỉnh của Pilar để kế thừa giấc mơ của cha họ.

source_en:
Everyone who crossed paths with Rebecca came away with the same take: loose cannon, hair-trigger temper. David knew that better than anyone; he'd lost count of the messes he'd had to scrub clean after her. To an outsider, she was a different breed of edgerunner. She didn't care about the payout or the risk—as long as a job didn't cross her moral line, she'd take it. Slip into whatever role the gig demanded. One night, she was the innocent girl caught in the crossfire; the next, a bored punk looking for trouble at a bar. But she always preferred being the muscle. Point the gun. Pull the trigger. Sort out the details once the smoke cleared. Her recklessness drove her partners up the wall, but nobody ever really hated her for it. Not when she had their backs every step of the way.
 
In Night City, surviving as an edgerunner takes more than a steady nerve; you need an edge that sets you apart. Maine had his hand cannon. Dorio, her fists. Kiwi had her tech. David had his Sandevistan, sure, but it didn't make him a killer. He was still a rookie, rough around the edges. He needed to learn how to handle iron, and he needed to learn fast. Rebecca was the natural choice to show him the way. As the crew's self-appointed weapons expert, she knew her guns like the back of her hand. On the range, she was surgical; in the streets, a bullet-storm of terror. When David realized he needed that extra bit of lethality to survive, she didn't hesitate. She threw him headfirst into the deep end. Walked him through every drill. Tried cramming a lifetime of survival know-how into the kid before the city could eat him alive.
new_translation_vi: Bất cứ ai từng gặp Rebecca đều có chung một nhận xét: một kẻ liều lĩnh, tính khí thất thường. David biết điều đó rõ hơn ai hết; anh đã không đếm xuể những mớ hỗn độn mà anh phải dọn dẹp sau cô. Đối với người ngoài, cô là một kiểu edgerunner khác biệt. Cô không quan tâm đến tiền thưởng hay rủi ro—miễn là công việc không vượt quá giới hạn đạo đức của cô, cô sẽ nhận. Nhập vai vào bất cứ vai trò nào mà phi vụ yêu cầu. Một đêm, cô là cô gái ngây thơ bị mắc kẹt trong làn đạn; đêm tiếp theo, một kẻ nổi loạn chán đời đang tìm kiếm rắc rối tại một quán bar. Nhưng cô luôn thích làm người cầm súng. Chĩa súng. Bóp cò. Giải quyết chi tiết sau khi khói tan. Sự liều lĩnh của cô khiến các đối tác phát điên, nhưng không ai thực sự ghét cô vì điều đó. Không phải khi cô luôn bảo vệ họ trong từng bước đi.

source_en:
Rebecca never bothered hiding it. She had feelings for David—plain and simple. But for someone who lived her life like a live grenade, she was surprisingly disciplined when it came to him. She kept a level head. She knew she'd never be the girl he pined for. No matter what gesture, angle, or trick she pulled to show him how she felt, it was obvious his heart would never be hers. But white flags were never in her playbook. If she couldn't have him, she'd pour all that energy into keeping him alive.
 
This was a task made all the harder—and more vital—after losing half her crew. One by one, familiar faces were reduced to cold names on a mausoleum wall. Even for a girl as tough as Rebecca, who had known loss all her life, it was too much to bear. She found a corner in a dead-end alley and emptied clip after clip into the dark, screaming curses like the noise could smother the grief clawing at her insides. Why had it turned out like this? Hadn't she paid enough? She didn't have a grand dream. She didn't care about becoming a legend. All she wanted—the only thing that mattered—was not to have to watch another person she loved flatline before her eyes.
 
So when David started loading up on chrome, carrying Maine's torch as if it were his alone to bear, she couldn't stop the dread from curling in her chest. A leader of a crew? Some hotshot merc with military-grade hardware? No. To her, he was still just a kid. A cocksure gonk with dreams big enough to swallow him whole. And Rebecca wasn't about to let that happen. Not without a fight. With new chrome arms built to handle heavy recoil, she stepped up as his second-in-command. Ready to be both his sword and shield. To make sure this fool she loved didn't get himself killed.
new_translation_vi: Rebecca chưa bao giờ bận tâm che giấu điều đó. Cô có tình cảm với David—đơn giản và rõ ràng. Nhưng đối với một người sống cuộc đời như một quả lựu đạn sống, cô lại vô cùng kỷ luật khi nói đến anh. Cô giữ một cái đầu lạnh. Cô biết mình sẽ không bao giờ là cô gái mà anh khao khát. Dù có cử chỉ, góc độ hay thủ thuật nào cô thực hiện để cho anh thấy cô cảm thấy thế nào, rõ ràng trái tim anh sẽ không bao giờ thuộc về cô. Nhưng cờ trắng chưa bao giờ nằm trong kế hoạch của cô. Nếu cô không thể có anh, cô sẽ dồn hết năng lượng đó để giữ anh sống sót.

source_en:
The fear Rebecca had carried all this time finally became a reality. Even with David's freakishly high tolerance, his body couldn't keep up with the chrome he kept stacking. That, combined with the weight of the choices he had to make, sent him sliding toward the edge of cyberpsychosis. She wanted him to go easy on himself, terrified for his mental state, but David always acted fast—just like her.
 
Their last gig was highly dangerous—if not impossible. But David insisted on having his way. Rebecca was furious, but there was no turning back. Only when it was too late did she realize the truth: they'd walked into a trap. Meticulously laid. Perfectly executed. They never suspected that their own crewmate had sold them out.
 
When they learned Lucy had been captured, David went out of his way—and out of his body—to get her back. It was a suicide mission, plain and simple. The dominoes were already falling, one bad call cascading into an avalanche of disaster. There was no time to untangle the mess. No time to second-guess. Rebecca grabbed her iron, looked at that idiot who was ready to risk everything for the woman he loved, and let out a long, tired sigh.
 
"...Fine. Sign me up, choomba. Into the fire."
 
Night City would never forget that night. Their ride speeding towards Arasaka Tower, MaxTac units spraying lead at them from both sides. David burning the Sandevistan. Again. Again. Again. To carry out a plan so reckless it might as well have been a one-way ticket. Rebecca had no choice but to support him—to make sure he made it to Corpo Plaza alive. All beneath the neon glow of Night City bleeding across the skyline.
 
Despite the odds, Rebecca held onto her hope.
 
She bet it all on Lucy. One last time, she loaded her love and courage into the chamber.
new_translation_vi: Nỗi sợ hãi mà Rebecca mang theo suốt thời gian qua cuối cùng đã trở thành hiện thực. Ngay cả với khả năng chịu đựng cao bất thường của David, cơ thể anh cũng không thể theo kịp lượng chrome mà anh liên tục chồng chất. Điều đó, kết hợp với sức nặng của những lựa chọn mà anh phải thực hiện, đã đẩy anh trượt dần về phía bờ vực của chứng rối loạn tâm thần mạng. Cô muốn anh nhẹ nhàng với bản thân, sợ hãi cho trạng thái tinh thần của anh, nhưng David luôn hành động nhanh chóng—giống như cô.

source_en:
After finding herself in the Somnoire, Rebecca knew immediately that she was dead. She chose only to keep quiet about it to avoid putting that weight on Lucy.
 
"Saying it would only have twisted Lucy up even more. If she started feelin' guilty or sorry for me, that'd just piss me off."
 
On the train tearing through the dream dimension, Rebecca shrugged and fed rounds into her iron, one by one. Outside the window, stars bled past—as bright and blinding as the neon that had once painted the Night City sky. She was on her way to save someone. Same old story. She was still fighting for Lucy, someone she couldn't understand but couldn't stop admiring, either. But this time, David wasn't beside her. And the girl they were going to save wasn't running away anymore.
 
She hated admitting it, but somewhere along the ride, she'd figured out why she was really here. Even if David hadn't asked, she still would've picked up her gun and gone after that pain-in-the-ass netrunner. She was part of the crew. And the crew were the chooms Rebecca cared about the most.
 
Choose her own path, make her own decisions—it's all she ever wanted. And she's gonna keep doing exactly that. No matter the risk, she will jump into fire if needed to save her friends.
 
"A flying train, a talking kitty-cat, you and Abby... Heh, this crew of ours is scary stacked."
 
"I told you, I'm not a cat, meow... And don't forget, the goal is to recover the Dream Band..."
 
"Relax, I got it memorized! We turn that chrome-dome into scrap metal, right?"
 
"You didn't catch a word, did you..."
 
Rebecca flashed a crooked grin and scratched the white cat behind the ear, shoving her hands in her pockets as she plopped down next to you. Rover.
 
"So, uh… kinda late to say sorry for dragging you into this, huh?"
 
A fist bump. That was all it took for her to know she was forgiven. Rebecca smirked, swung Guts onto her shoulder, and strolled up to the train doors.
 
"End of the line! Let's go do what we came here to do!"
new_translation_vi: Sau khi thấy mình ở trong Somnoire, Rebecca biết ngay rằng mình đã chết. Cô chọn giữ im lặng về điều đó để tránh đặt gánh nặng đó lên Lucy.

source_en:
Lucy keeps most of her past to herself for a reason. Few know that this mysterious netrunner was, in fact, shown the ropes by a top-secret Arasaka educational program for kids. One might say that's not the worst hand to be dealt; that a roof over your head and a full belly is more than many can hope for in Night City. But for Lucy, there was never any other path. She was brought up in this megacorp's black site—locked away and forced to train. Day after day, year after year, breaching the Blackwall, diving into the scattered depths of the Old Net. And trying to survive the rogue AIs that lurked there.
 
As a child, Lucy's worldview was built upon Arasaka's core pillar: obedience—often mistaken for loyalty. And she was not the only one taught to believe in it. A group of children took part in the program, either taken from their parents or scooped from the street. To serve the most powerful corporation on the planet—that was the dream Arasaka planted in their heads. Within that facility, they were forced to deep-dive the Old Net, running suicide gigs on repeat. None of them knew the perfect future they'd been promised was just a chimera. An elaborate fantasy spun by Arasaka handlers to serve the company's own ends. By the time Lucy figured out the truth, it was already too late.
 
The will to survive drove them to claw their way out of the prison they had long mistaken for home. They ran as fast as they could, bullets tearing through the air all around them. Gunfire and screams exploded in Lucy's ears, one after another. But she would survive. She squeezed her eyes shut, blocked everything out, and just kept running. The exit. She just had to reach the exit.
 
She woke up in some scrapyard with no memory of how she got there, and no idea if anyone else had made it out alive. She'd escaped the chase, for now, but the fear Arasaka had carved into her wasn't going anywhere. She knew they'd be hunting her. Could feel it under her skin. After that, she never stayed in one place for too long. Always moving. Always hiding.
new_translation_vi: Lucy giữ hầu hết quá khứ của mình cho riêng mình vì một lý do. Ít ai biết rằng netrunner bí ẩn này, thực tế, đã được đào tạo bởi một chương trình giáo dục tối mật của Arasaka dành cho trẻ em. Người ta có thể nói đó không phải là một ván bài tồi tệ nhất; rằng một mái nhà trên đầu và một cái bụng no là điều mà nhiều người ở Night City không dám hy vọng. Nhưng đối với Lucy, chưa bao giờ có con đường nào khác. Cô được nuôi dưỡng trong khu vực đen của tập đoàn này—bị nhốt và buộc phải huấn luyện. Ngày qua ngày, năm qua năm, xâm nhập Blackwall, lặn sâu vào những chiều sâu phân tán của Old Net. Và cố gắng sống sót trước những AI nổi loạn ẩn nấp ở đó.

source_en:
It started with a poster: a man in a spacesuit, pointing the way to a better future. For Lucy, it was a promise of escape. And maybe, just maybe, finding a place so far away from danger that she could stay put. On countless nights, curled up with her arms wrapped around her knees, that dream took root. Planted by fear. Loneliness. A need for a place to call home.

"Maybe on the Moon, I'll finally be free?"

Cynics laughed at the idea, certain there was no corner safe from corporate dominance. To go there would be pointless; a propaganda-fuelled pipe dream. But these were the opinions of people who had never been to the Moon. So what did they know? Lucy would go there. See for herself. Someday.

Night City seemed like a good place to hide for a while. A concrete jungle. When she first arrived, she feared Arasaka's reach was too prominent, but soon she learned to haunt the corners of the city where corporations turned a blind eye. She realized that crime and violence were the true governors here. And with her skill set and caution, she was natural merc material. An edgerunner already long in the making. Her new home wasn't completely safe for her, but for the first time in years, she felt like she could survive.

Erasing every trace of her past became her new identity. To stay alive without blowing her cover, the former netrunner prodigy lived by a simple code: Stay low. Ask nothing. Tell less. Avoid Arasaka. That was her disguise. A small principle, but it was hers. Life only truly changed when Kiwi came looking for a preem netrunner to fill a slot in Maine's crew. She brought Lucy into the fold and gave her the most useful advice she'd ever get:

"Remember. Never trust a soul in Night City."

Và có lẽ, chỉ có lẽ thôi, tìm được một nơi xa xôi đến mức nguy hiểm không thể chạm tới để cô có thể ở lại. Trong vô số đêm, cuộn tròn với đôi tay ôm lấy đầu gối, giấc mơ đó đã bén rễ. Được gieo mầm bởi nỗi sợ hãi. Sự cô đơn. Một nhu cầu về một nơi để gọi là nhà.

source_en:
One night, Lucy took David to her place and invited him to experience a braindance of the Moon. Since she couldn't afford to travel there yet, this was the closest she could get to the real deal. Feeling the sun on her face. Jumping and floating like a feather. Serenity. Without corpos, without gangers. It was the most precious part of herself she could share.

She couldn't deny that David piqued her interest. An Arasaka Academy dropout with the reckless ambition to become an edgerunner. Wielding extremely demanding—extremely dangerous—military-grade cyberware as if it were a toy. But he was a good kid, sincere, pure at heart. Someone she felt she could possibly trust. But Lucy had spent so long keeping the world at arm's length that she didn't know how to reach out.

After David joined Maine's crew, Lucy grumbled about being saddled with babysitting duty. But despite her protests, she took him under her wing. Became his first teacher on the streets of Night City. She showed him the ropes of a merc's day-to-day, assuming he wouldn't be cut out for the life. But as she watched the boy come into his own, the knot in her chest finally started to loosen.

Her certainty about him came the day he saved her life.

A routine night turned into a bloodbath. When Pilar fell, the crew shattered into a blur of instinct and rage. Hot-headed members like Rebecca threw themselves at the killer, while Lucy took cover to strike with caution. In the chaos, David froze. Unable to move, to fight, or even save himself. But through the mayhem, he was the only one to notice Lucy being cornered. That was all the motivation he needed. In an instant, he lunged into the fray, guns blazing. To save her.

Bang.

Smoke. Silence. A turning point for both of them.

After that, Lucy led him to the rooftop—the place where she'd always gone to look at the Moon. For the first time, she didn't go alone. She brought a boy who had nothing, who promised her everything.

He told her he'd take her there. To the Moon. Someday, somehow. A promise that burned brighter and felt more real than any neon in the city below.

So how could she not love him?

source_en:
Some say that tragedy is the only truth in Night City. That happiness is just fleeting smoke.

Maine and Dorio fell on a job gone sideways. David picked up the weight. Took over the crew. Maine's legacy. The life of an edgerunner. Rebecca switched to stronger cyber-arms and swore she'd never lose anyone else. Everyone moved forward.

Everyone, except Lucy.

She stepped back. Pulled away from the crew and secretly worked to protect David from the shadows, making sure Arasaka couldn't trace him. She told no one. Especially not him. She knew David would try to stop her, or worse, follow her into the fire. That was his nature. He was obsessed with protecting her. But for once, Lucy was determined to be the one holding the shield.

She was careful, but as it turned out, not careful enough. She'd underestimated Arasaka. Their fixer, Faraday, saw the opening. Found the crack in the armor. And in it, he discovered a way to exploit the love between two edgerunners to secure his ticket up the corpo ladder.

Having snatched Lucy, Faraday forced David into a desperate rescue mission as the boy teetered on the edge of cyberpsychosis. David didn't give up, not even with MaxTac hot on his heels. Rebecca and Falco—the remains of a loyal crew—threw themselves into the line of fire just to keep him moving.

The cyberskeleton did its job. David got Lucy out... only to fall into a trap set by Arasaka. A trap with Adam Smasher waiting inside.

David held Lucy close and jumped towards the Moon, which hung cold and white above the chaos. In that moment, her kiss pulled him back from the edge. Just long enough. Just enough for a final goodbye.

source_en:
Rebecca and David were gone. Only Lucy and Falco survived that day. The two of them split ways after leaving Night City, and when the dust settled, it was time to move on again.
 
There was only one place she considered her destination. A too-obvious choice. A promise, never fulfilled. Did she go there to honor it, to make a dream come true, or to hide away for good? Lucy found herself on the Moon with no answers.
 
The real experience was different than the one from the braindance, and yet, the place had felt somehow familiar. For a moment, she could've sworn she saw David out of the corner of her eye. That was when the grief finally broke through. The Moon was still the same, but the boy who'd been beside her in the braindance wasn't there anymore.
 
Yet, maybe the story wasn't over.
 
"There… is a method. To let you stay."
 
On the day she left the Somnoire, Lucy stopped at the threshold of the gateway and turned to Rover. Took one last look at the silent Moon beyond.
 
"That's not what they would've wanted, is it?"

Sprawled under the bushes are the bodies from last night's gang war. I didn't know the man, but I recognized the gun tucked in his waistband.

Most of the gun frame was stained red, but those pinstripes, the matte finish grip... There's no mistaking it. That's my handiwork.

I modded that gun two months ago. It was a rush order. Owner was flush with cash and had specific demands. He wanted me to use the best paint money could buy to ink his favorite rock star—clutching a guitar while flipping the bird—onto the frame. To show he meant business, he gave me a huge deposit, which I repaid in three days and nights of work... Shame, really. I kinda liked that piece.

As a gang "cleaner," Parker had no choice. His life was on standby, always on call to mop up the bossman's mess.

After a brisk, cold shower, Parker left home. True to his routine, he circled the block three times in a ride rented under a fake ID before finally heading to the destination. Body Heat Radio was playing his favorite track. Parker headbanged like a psycho. Cars behind sounded off at his erratic driving, but he didn't give a damn.

"This is the last one, Parker. Finish this job and you're done. Take the eddies and fly, far away."

He couldn't have known that a year ago, his predecessor had been humming this exact tune on the same road, speeding to the final job of her life.

"Let me go Ponpon-shiru, let me go Ponpon-shiru!"

source_en:
Richard was old, so old he could no longer remember exactly what his gang sign looked like.

But his body remembered. Richard's newly installed cybernetic tendons fluidly executed the dodge command he issued. An onyx blade pierced a throat and exited through the skull. With a purposeful slash, a coolant-soaked brainstem explodes into a work of modern art.

Sheathing his blade, Richard turned back. He pulled a pair of reading glasses from his coat and wiped them with a clean corner of his shirt.

"Maelstrom lackeys... Guess I got the wrong guys."

Richard scratched his head and spat at the dead punk, then he pushed his glasses back into place.

He wanted Kiroshi optics, but his body rejected ocular implants. The Immunoblocker shots required to keep them riddled his body with track marks in just a few days. Left with no choice, Richard went back to his "original part," donning reading glasses while plying his trade.

"Now, where did those five Animals run off to..."

Hugging the wall, Richard followed the trail left by his inside man, stepping ever deeper into the dark alley.

"Hang in there, Richard. Kill 'em quick, and go home early."
